A character aboard a starship can fill one of several possible roles, which determines what the character can do.
Commander: A ship’s commander makes decisions about tactics and issues orders to the crew. The commander
can help another crewmember by taking an aid another action. The commander must be located on the starship’s
command deck to do so.
Aiding another crewmember is a move action. A starship can only have one commander, and ships under
Colossal size tend not to have a commander at all.
Pilot: The pilot of a starship controls its movement. Most starships have only one position from which the starship
can be piloted. Piloting a starship is always at least a move action, which means that the pilot may be able to do
something else with her attack action each round. On smaller ships such as fighters, the pilot also serves as the
gunner. A starship can have only one pilot at a time. It is the pilot who ultimately decides how the starship moves.
Copilot: The copilot can help the pilot on Pilot checks by taking an aid another action. The copilot must be located 666
somewhere on the ship from where he can see the starship’s surroundings and advise the pilot (usually the
command deck or cockpit). Aiding the pilot is a move action, leaving the copilot with an attack action each round
to do something else. A copilot may also serve as a gunner or sensor operator if he can access one of the starship’s
weapon systems or the ship’s sensors from his station. A starship can have only one copilot at a time.
Gunner: A gunner controls one of the ship’s weapon systems, applying her ranged attack bonus and Dexterity
modifier to the attack rolls. A ship with multiple weapon systems can have multiple gunners.
Sensor Operator: Although the copilot usually operates the sensors, some ships (particularly heavy and
superheavy ships) have a dedicated crew position for a sensor operator. A sensor operator can take an aid another
action either to help the pilot with Pilot checks, or to help a gunner with attack rolls. Either is a move action,
leaving the sensor operator with an attack action each round to do something else. A starship can have as many
sensor operators as it has different sensor systems (see Starship Sensors).
Engineer: A starship’s engineer keeps the ship in working order. If a system has failed for any reason, it is usually
up to the engineer to get that system working again. An engineer can attempt a Repair check to fix minor problems
as a full round action. A starship can have one engineer, plus one additional engineer each for the ship’s life
support, sensors (and communications), and defensive systems.
Passenger: All other personnel aboard the starship are considered passengers for purposes of starship combat.
Passengers have no specific role in the starship’s operation, but they help repel boarders or take other actions.

A starship is typically and almost always of the following types: Gargantuan (ultralight), Colossal (ultralight),
Colossal (light), Colossal (mediumweight), Colossal (heavy), or Colossal (superheavy). A starship’s type determines
how much space it occupies on the battle grid, as well as its game statistics.
To build a starship hull from scratch, a character must succeed at a Craft (structural) check (DC 30) after
investing the requisite amount of assembly time, based on the ship’s type: Gargantuan 300 hours, Colossal
(ultralight) 600 hours, Colossal (light) 1,200 hours, Colossal (mediumweight) 2,400 hours, Colossal (heavy) 4,800
hours, Colossal (superheavy) 9,600 hours. A character without a mechanical tool kit takes a –4 penalty on the skill 667
check. The character must also spend Wealth equal to the ship’s base purchase DC.

This chapter includes ready-to-use templates and statistics for various starship subtypes of each Tech Scale (TS).
These statistics represent baseline models only. A starship’s statistics and performance can be improved by
upgrading its weapons, armor, shields, defensive systems, and engines.
Each starship description includes the following statistics.
Type: The starship’s type (ultralight, light, mediumweight, heavy, or superheavy) determines its maximum weapon
size and fighting space on the battle grid.
Size / Space: The ship’s size affects its Armor Class, weapon attack rolls, and grapple modifier; the ship’s space on
the battle grid is based on the ship’s type. The size of the ship on a 250-foot hex map is given as either “1 hex” for
Ultralight and smaller starships, or “n-polyhex” where “n” is the number of 250-foot hexes per side of the larger
polyhex used to represent that ship. Light-Colossal starships occupy a 2-polyhex space, a larger hex space that is
two (2) 250-foot hexes per side, occupying a total of 7 (1 central plus the 6 surrounding) 250-foot hexes.
Mediumweight starships occupy a 3-polyhex space, a total of 19 (1 central plus the 6 surrounding plus the 12
surrounding those 6) 250-foot hexes. Heavy starships occupy a 4-polyhex space, a total of (1 central plus the 6
hexes surrounding plus the 12 hexes surrounding those 6 plus the 18 hexes surrounding those 12 hexes equals)
thirty-seven (37) 250-foot hexes. Superheavy starships occupy 5-polyhex and larger spaces (see individual starship
descriptions for more details). The number of the polyhex for a starship is how many 250-foot hexes of movement
the ship must spend in order to turn to face an adjacent side (a turn of 60’). Gargantuan and smaller starships (i.e.,
starships considered microhex on the stellar-scale hex grid) have no movement cost to turn.
Subtype: The starship’s subtype describes the ship’s primary function (for example, fighter or strike cruiser).
Tactical Speed: Tactical speed represents how far the starship can move as a move action using its thrusters.
Speed is listed in feet and hexes. Most starships have a base tactical speed of 3,000 feet (12 hexes). Better engines
can improve a starship’s tactical speed (see Starship Engines), while heavier armor can reduce a ship’s tactical
speed (see Starship Armor,).
Touch/Full AC (T/AC): A starship’s touch Armor Class (the first number) determines how hard the ship is to hit. A
starship’s total Armor Class (the second number) determines how hard the ship is to critically hit. A starship’s flat-
footed Armor Class does not include the pilot’s Dexterity modifier. A starship’s autopilot touch Armor Class is used
when the ship’s autopilot system is engaged.
Length / Weight: The ship’s length in feet, and its weight in pounds or tons.
Hardness: A ship’s hardness is determined by its armor, presented in hit points, dice (“d”), and capital dice (“D”).
Hardness reduces the amount of damage the ship takes from weapon attacks. Better armor can improve a ship’s
hardness.
Crew: The ship’s standard crew complement is given here. A ship cannot operate with less than one-quarter of its
standard crew complement. The crew’s quality is given in parentheses, along with the crew’s modifier to skill
checks (including Pilot checks made to avoid hazards). The quality of the crew determines the pilot’s Defense
bonus, the pilot’s Dexterity modifier, and the gunner’s attack bonus (see Table: Crew Quality for details).
Hit Dice: A ship’s Hit Dice, presented in capital dice, (“D”) determines how much damage the starship can sustain.
Hit Dice are never rolled to determine a starship’s hit points; the ship always gets the maximum 20 hit points for
each Hit Die (“Capital Die”). The number in brackets is the number of capital dice per each of the starship’s section
Passenger Capacity: The maximum number of passengers that can be safely lodged aboard the ship.
Initiative Modifier: A starship’s initiative modifier is equal to the pilot’s Dexterity modifier, plus any other relevant
initiative based modifiers, such as a +4 bonus if the pilot has the Improved Initiative feat or certain sensor arrays.
Cargo Capacity: The maximum tonnage of cargo that the ship can store in its holds.
Pilot’s Dex Modifier: The pilot’s Dexterity modifier applies to the starship’s touch Armor Class, except when the
ship is flat-footed or grappled. The maximum Dex modifier available is equal to 1 plus the Class of the sensor array
used by the starship (up to a maximum +10 Dex modifier for a 30 or higher Dex with a Class IX Sensor Array).
Gunner’s Attack Bonus: The gunner’s attack bonus applies to ranged weapon attacks.
Pilot’s Defense Bonus: The pilot’s Defense Bonus (if any) applies to the starship’s full Armor Class, as well as any
dodge or grapple attempts.
Grapple Modifier: These modifiers are used in starship-to-starship grappling, with the modifier in parentheses 668
applying to smaller scale (Gargantuan and smaller) targets. The ship’s grapple check modifier is based on its size
(Gargantuan [ultralight] +0, Colossal [ultralight +4, light +8, mediumweight +12, heavy +16, superheavy +20]).
Grapple checks come into play whenever grapplers and tractor beams are used (see Grappling Systems).
Base Purchase DC: The base purchase DC includes the ship’s hull and a trained crew (see Crew, above), but not its
engines, armor, shields, defensive systems, sensor systems, comm systems, weapons, or grappling systems (which
must be purchased separately).
Restriction: The ship’s restriction rating.
Upgraded Purchase DC: This is the total cost of a typical model starship as given in the template. This cost does
not include the Restriction modifier if the starship is being purchased on the market.
Targeting System Bonus: The ship’s computerized targeting system provides an equipment bonus on a gunner’s
attack rolls and a similar equipment bonus on attack rolls made by the ship’s point-defense system.
Standard Design Specs: The ship’s engines, armor, defensive systems, sensors, communications, weapons, and
grappling systems are listed here.
Engines: Most starships have two engine systems.
Armor: All starships have one type of armor, providing the starship’s Hardness and total Armor Class.
Defensive Systems: These systems provide defensive bonuses to the starship, and most ships will have 4-8 such
systems.
Sensors: The eyes and ears of the starship, most starships have two sensor systems, with the largest ships
sometimes having three sensor systems.
Communications: All starships can have up to two communications systems.
Weapons & Grappling Systems: Weapons systems fall into several categories; ballistic weapons, energy weapons,
missiles, mines, and grappling systems.
IMPROVING A STARSHIP’S STATISTICS
The starship statistics presented below use standard design specs appropriate for the lowest Tech Scale at which
these ships can be played (TS 6 or TS 7 for most ships). Improving a starship’s statistics requires upgrades to its
crew, armor, defensive systems, sensor systems, and/or weapons, as discussed throughout this chapter.

Ultralight ships cover most small spacecraft, including starfighters, cutters, launches, and couriers. An ultralight
starship can be up to 250 feet long. It occupies a 250-foot-by-250-foot fighting space, 1 hex on the stellar scale,
and up to five ultralight starships can occupy a single 250-foot space. Due to their relatively small size, ultralight
starships can form into wings (see Ultralight Starship Wings).
In addition, all ultralight starships share the following design specs.
Engines: All ultralight starships have thrusters. In addition, ships of TS 6 or higher have one other type of engine
(see Starship Engines).
Armor: All starships have one type of armor (see Starship Armor).
Defensive Systems: An ultralight starship has a maximum of one defensive system per 3 Hit Dice (see Starship
Defense Systems).
Sensors: An ultralight starship has a maximum of two sensor systems (see Starship Sensors).
Communications: An ultralight starship has a maximum of two external communication systems (see Starship
Comm Systems).
Weapons: An ultralight starship has one beam, projectile, or missile weapon per 3 Hit Dice (see Starship Weapons).
These weapons are often fire-linked. An ultralight ship cannot be armed with mines.
Grappling Systems: An ultralight starship may have up to two grappling systems (see Grappling Systems). Each
grappling system takes away one of the ship’s weapon slots (see above).

polyhex 6 hexes in length on each side). Thus, the Dreadnought and the Star Carrier, both falling into the 2,501-
