Aura (Ex): A Cleric of a chaotic, evil, good, or lawful deity has a particularly powerful aura corresponding to the deity’s alignment (see the Detect Alignment spell for details). Clerics who don’t worship a specific deity but choose the Chaotic, Evil, Good, or Lawful domain have a similarly powerful aura of the corresponding alignment. Spells: A Cleric casts divine spells, which are drawn from the Cleric spell list. However, their alignment may restrict them from casting certain spells opposed to their moral or ethical beliefs; see Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells, below. A Cleric must choose and prepare their spells in advance (see below). A 1st-level Cleric begins with access to the 1st-level Cleric spell list. To prepare or cast a spell, a Cleric must 82 have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level, and they must be of the minimum level capable of casting the spell (ie. 3rd-level Cleric for 2nd-level Cleric spell access, 5th-level Cleric for 3rd-level Cleric spell access, etc.). The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a Cleric’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the Cleric’s Wisdom modifier. Like other spellcasters, a Cleric can cast only a certain number of spells per day. Their base daily divine power point allotment is given on Table: Cleric Class Statistics by Level. In addition, they receive bonus spell points per day if they have a Wisdom score of 12 or higher. A Cleric must also memorize one domain spell of each spell level they can cast, starting at 1st level. When a Cleric prepares their spells for the day, at least one spell of each spell level the Cleric has access to must be a domain spell; at least one spell per spell level per day must come from one of their two domains (see Domains, under Spells & Powers, below). Clerics meditate or pray for their spells. Each Cleric must choose a time at which they must spend 1 hour each day in quiet contemplation or supplication to regain their daily allotment of spell points. Time spent resting has no effect on whether a Cleric can prepare spells. A Cleric may prepare and cast any spell on the Cleric spell list, provided that they can cast spells of that level, but they must choose which spells to prepare during their daily meditation. Deity, Domains, and Domain Spells: A Cleric’s deity influences their alignment, what magic they can perform, their values, and how others see them. A Cleric chooses two domains from among those belonging to their deity. A Cleric can select an alignment domain (Chaos, Evil, Good, or Law) only if their own alignment matches that domain. Conversely, a Cleric with at least one Neutral aspect of their alignment can spend both their domains to take the Druid option (see below). If a Cleric is not devoted to a particular deity, they still select two domains to represent their spiritual inclinations and abilities. The restriction on alignment domains still applies. Each domain gives the Cleric access to a domain spell at each spell level they can cast, from 1st on up, as well as a granted power. The Cleric gets the granted powers of both the domains selected. With access to two domain spells at a given spell level, a Cleric prepares at least one or the other each day as their obligatory domain spell for each spell level. Spontaneous Casting: A good Cleric (or a neutral Cleric of a good deity) can channel stored spell energy into healing spells that the Cleric did not prepare ahead of time. The Cleric can “lose” any prepared spell that is not a domain spell in order to cast any Cure spell of the same spell level or lower (a Cure spell is any spell with “Cure” in its name). An evil Cleric (or a neutral Cleric of an evil deity), can’t convert prepared spells to Cure spells but can convert them to Inflict spells (an Inflict spell is one with “Inflict” in its name). A Cleric who is neither good nor evil and whose deity is neither good nor evil can convert spells to either Cure spells or Inflict spells (player’s choice). Once the player makes this choice, it cannot be reversed. This choice also determines whether the Cleric turns or commands undead (see below). Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells: A Cleric can’t cast spells of an alignment opposed to their own or their deity’s (if they have one). Spells associated with particular alignments are indicated by the chaos, evil, good, and law descriptors in their spell descriptions. Turn or Rebuke Undead (Su): Any Cleric, regardless of alignment, has the power to affect undead creatures by channeling the power of their faith through their holy (or unholy) symbol (see Turn or Rebuke Undead under Combat, below). A good Cleric (or a neutral Cleric who worships a good deity) can turn or destroy undead creatures. An evil Cleric (or a neutral Cleric who worships an evil deity) instead rebukes or commands such creatures. A neutral Cleric of a neutral deity must choose whether their turning ability functions as that of a good Cleric or an evil Cleric. Once this choice is made, it cannot be reversed. This decision also determines whether the Cleric can cast spontaneous Cure or Inflict spells (see above). A Cleric may attempt to turn undead a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Charisma modifier. A Cleric with 5+ ranks in Knowledge (religion) gets a +2 bonus on turning checks against undead. Bonus Languages: A Cleric’s bonus language options include Celestial, Abyssal, and Infernal (the languages of good, chaotic evil, and lawful evil outsiders, respectively). Esoteric Knowledge: At 2nd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th levels, the Cleric learns some obscure information related to a Knowledge skill; receive a +1 competence bonus on one Knowledge skill in which the character has 1 or more 83 ranks. Note that the competence bonus may be applied to the same Knowledge skill or different Knowledge skills, but once it is selected, it cannot be changed. Expanded Domain: At 8th and 16th level, the Cleric can petition their god to grant them one spell or power not normally available to the Cleric as a new Domain spell. The spell or power in question must relate to one of the Cleric’s domains (GM’s judgment), and if the petition is granted then the spell or power becomes a domain spell for the Cleric. Additional Domain: At 19th level, the Cleric becomes a more complete representative of their god, gaining access to the granted power and domain spell list of another one of their god’s domains. If their god has no new domain to offer the character, then they gain a bonus Magic feat instead. Bonus Feat: At 4th, 12th, and 20th levels, the Cleric gets to select a bonus feat from the Magic feat list. They must meet any prerequisites necessary in order to select the feat. Ex-Clerics (“Excommunicatus”): A Cleric who grossly violates the code of conduct required by their god loses all spells and class features, except for armor and shield proficiencies and proficiency with simple weapons. They cannot thereafter gain levels as a divine spellcaster of that god until they atone (see the Atonement spell description). The Druid Option A priest of nature, a Druid is a specialized Cleric who reveres the concept of balance as a natural norm. If a player wishes, they may give up their ability to turn undead and both of their Domain choices to instead make their Cleric a Druid. If you do, then apply the following rules to the generation of your Druid; anything not expressly mentioned is the same as the Cleric. Prerequisite: As a worshipper of nature in some way, the Druid must have an aspect of their alignment that is expressly neutral; thus, alignment options are (true) Neutral, Chaotic/Neutral, Lawful/Neutral, Neutral/Evil, or Neutral/Good. However, unlike other Clerics, the Druid does not require a minimum Tech Scale 1 scenario. Skills: Add Knowledge (nature) and Survival to the list of Cleric class skills for your Druid. Feats: Druids are not allowed to wield any metal weapons, or wear any metal armor, except for those weapons that are implements of the field (ie. a sickle or scythe). They do not have proficiency with them as weapons, only that they are permitted to use them. A Druid that wields metal weapons of war or wears metal armor loses all access to their Druid spells until they stop using the prohibited equipment and perform an Atonement. Class Features: Aura: Because of their philosophy of balance, Druids do not have the typical Aura that Clerics do. Divine Spells: A Druid has access to a specialized list of spells, based on their focus in natural magic. See the Druid’s spell list for more details. They are otherwise identical to Clerics in how they receive and memorize spells. Deity, Domain, and Domain Spells: Your GM can help you determine which deity your character worships (if not “Mother Nature”). As mentioned earlier, it costs your Cleric both Domain choices and the ability to Turn Undead to select the Druid option. Instead, the Druid has access to the Druid spell list. Spontaneous Casting: Instead of the spontaneous casting of a Cleric into Cure spells (for a good Cleric) or Inflict spells (for an evil Cleric), A Druid can spontaneously convert any spell they have memorized into the equivalent- level version of Summon Nature’s Ally, “losing” any prepared spell in order to cast a Summon Nature’s Ally spell of the same spell level or lower. Animal Companion (Ex): At 1st level, a Druid gains an animal companion selected from the following list: badger, camel, dire rat, dog, riding dog, eagle, hawk, horse (light or heavy), owl, pony, snake (Small or Medium viper), or wolf. If the campaign takes place wholly or partly in an aquatic environment, the following creatures may be added to the Druid’s list of options: crocodile, porpoise, Medium shark, and squid. This animal is a loyal companion that accompanies the Druid on adventures as appropriate for its kind. See the section below on Animal Companions and Familiars. Wild Empathy (Ex): From 1st level, a Druid can improve the attitude of an animal. This ability functions just like a Diplomacy check made to improve the attitude of a person. The Druid rolls 1d20 and adds their Druid level and their Charisma modifier to determine the wild empathy check result. The typical domestic animal has a starting attitude of indifferent, while wild animals are usually unfriendly. 84 To use wild empathy, the Druid and the animal must be able to study each other, which means that they must be within 30 feet of one another under normal conditions. Generally, influencing an animal in this way takes 1 minute but, as with influencing people, it might take more or less time. A Druid can also use this ability to influence a magical beast with an Intelligence score of 1 or 2, but they take a –4 penalty on the check. Woodland Stride (Ex): Starting at 3rd level, a Druid may move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at their normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. However, thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that are enchanted or magically manipulated to impede motion still affect them. Wildshape (Sp): Once a Druid reaches 5th level and gains access to 3rd-level spells, then they can also spontaneously convert any spell of equivalent level or higher to manifest Wildshape (see Metamorphosis for more details), as a spell-like ability equal to the character’s level. Ex-Druids: A Druid who ceases to revere nature, changes to a prohibited alignment, or teaches the Druidic language to a nondruidic spellcaster, loses all spells and Druid abilities (including their animal companion, but not including weapon, armor, and shield proficiencies). They cannot thereafter gain levels as a Druid until they atone (see the Atonement spell description). Starting Feats: In addition to the two feats all characters get at 1st level, an Expert begins play with Simple Weapons Proficiency feat and Light Armour Proficiency feat. Fighter Where there are conflicts, there are Fighters. More of a catch-all category than a formal title, a Fighter is one who focuses their education on the martial arts, developing their own unique fighting style in the process. Hit Die (of the Hero): d10 (d5+5) Action Points: Fighters gain a number of Action Points equal to their Charisma modifier [minimum +0, maximum +5] + one-half their character level, rounded down, at 1st level and every time they attain a new level in this class. Class Skills: The Fighter’s class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are: Balance (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Drive (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Jump (Str), Knowledge (tactics) (Int), Navigate (Int), Pilot (Dex), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Swim (Str), and Tumble (Dex). The Starting Occupation the character selects can provide additional class skills to choose from. Skill Points at 1st Level: (4 + Int modifier) x5. Skill Points at Each Additional Level: 4 + Int modifier. Starting Feats: In addition to the two feats all characters get at 1st level, a Fighter begins play with Simple Weapons Proficiency feat, Martial Weapons Proficiency feat, Light Armour Proficiency feat, Medium Armour Proficiency feat, Heavy Armour Proficiency feat, Shield Proficiency feat, and Tower Shield Proficiency feat. Monk The Monk is a student of an esoteric martial art, formally studied under the training of a monastery or master. While there are many such styles, they all focus on tapping one’s internal energy to be able to accomplish supernatural feats of strength and endurance. Prerequisite: Lawful alignment. Hit Die (of the Hero): d8 (d4+4) Action Points: Monks gain a number of Action Points equal to their Charisma modifier [minimum +0, maximum +5] + one-half their character level, rounded down, at 1st level and every time they attain a new level in this class. Class Skills: The Monk’s class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are: Autohypnosis (Wis), Balance (Dex), Climb (Str), Concentration (Con), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Hide (Dex), Jump (Str), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (psionics) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Knowledge (theology and philosophy) (Int), Listen (Wis), Move Silently (Dex), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Spot (Wis), Swim (Str), and Tumble (Dex). The Starting Occupation the character selects can provide additional class skills to choose from. Skill Points at 1st Level: (4 + Int modifier) x5. Skill Points at Each Additional Level: 4 + Int modifier. Starting Feats: In addition to the two feats all characters get at 1st level, a Monk begins play with the Simple 87 Weapons Proficiency feat, Combat Martial Arts, and Defensive Martial Arts. Flurry of Blows (Ex): The Monk has the virtual feat Two-Weapon Fighting when using only unarmed attacks, or a quarterstaff, and unarmored. First Degree Belt: The Monk has developed some aspect of their martial arts style; select from among Elusive Target, Improved Grapple, Nerve Pinch, or Stunning Fist. Evasion: The character avoids taking any damage on a successful Reflex save for half damage. Second Degree Belt: The Monk’s style continues to develop; select from among Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Combat Throw, or Deflect Arrows. The Monk need not have any of the prerequisites normally required for these feats to select them when chosen as a “Degree Belt”. Still Mind (Ex): A Monk of 3rd level of higher gains a +2 bonus on saving throws against spells and effects with the mind-affecting descriptor while focused (see Concentration skill). Wild Talent: The Monk’s self-mastery has resulted in the development of what some call “ki” or “chi”, effectively becoming a psionic character with 2 PP and access to the Power feat list. As a psionic character the Monk can become psionically focused with a full round Concentration check (see Concentration skill). Ki Strike: Magic (Su): The Monk’s mastery of ki now infuses their unarmed attacks. While focused, the Monk’s unarmed attacks are considered magical for purposes of damage reduction, and they ignore 5 points of hardness with their unarmed strikes. Slow Fall (Ex): The Monk can slow a fall to reduce the effective distance fallen. As long as the Monk is within 10’ of a wall, they can reduce the damage suffered by the fall by an amount equal to the distance given. At 4th level, the Monk can reduce the damage suffered by a fall by 2d6 (the amount suffered from a 20’ fall), as long as the Monk is within 10’ of a wall during the fall. In effect, the Monk uses the wall to slow their descent. A Monk of 20th level can fall any distance, as long as the Monk is within 10’ of a wall for the length of the fall. 88 Purity of Body (Ex): The Monk gains greater control of their internal processes. The Monk becomes immune to disease (but not supernatural and magical diseases) and gains the Speed of Thought virtual feat. Third Degree Belt: The Monk’s personal style develops further; select from among Improved Disarm, Improved Trip, Sidestep Charge, or Unbalance Opponent. The Monk need not have any of the prerequisites normally required for these feats to select them when chosen as a “Degree Belt”. Wholeness of Body (Ex): The Monk is able to heal their own wounds, capable of healing a number of hit points equal to twice their Monk level, spread out over several partial applications if desired. Power Fist: The Monk gains the Power Fist feat; the Monk need not have any of the prerequisites normally required for the feat. Improved Evasion (Ex): The Monk’s evasion ability improves. They still take no damage on a successful Reflex saving throw against attacks, but henceforth they may expend their focus to take only half damage on a failed save. A helpless Monk cannot gain the benefit of improved evasion. Ki Strike: Lawful (Su): The manifestation of the Monk’s ki in their unarmed strikes reaches a new level; whenever the Monk is focused and makes a successful unarmed melee attack, they deal an extra 1d6 points of damage, and their attack is treated as a lawful attack for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Diamond Body (Su): The Monk gains immunity to poisons of all kinds. Greater Flurry: The Monk’s flurry of blows comes even faster now; the Monk gains an additional attack at their highest attack bonus when performing a full-round attack with their unarmed strikes. Abundant Step (Su): The Monk can slip magically between spaces, as if using the spell Dimension Door, once per day. Their caster level for this effect is one-half their Monk level (rounded down). Diamond Soul (Ex): The Monk gains spell resistance equal to their current Monk level + 10. In order to affect the Monk with a spell or psionic power, a manifester must get a result on a manifester level check (1d20 + manifester level) that equals or exceeds the Monk’s spell resistance. Greater Power Fist: The Monk gains the Greater Power Fist feat; the Monk need not have any of the prerequisites normally required for the feat. Quivering Palm (Su): The Monk can set up vibrations within the body of another creature that can thereafter be fatal if the Monk so desires. They can use this quivering palm attack once a week, they must be focused when making the attempt, and they must announce their intent before making their attack roll. Constructs, oozes, plants, undead, incorporeal creatures, and creatures immune to critical hits cannot be affected. Otherwise, if the Monk strikes successfully and the target takes damage from the blow, the Monk expends their focus and the quivering palm attack succeeds. Thereafter the Monk can try to slay the victim at any later time, as long as the attempt is made within a number of days equal to the Monk’s class level. To make such an attempt, the Monk merely wills the target to die (a free action), and unless the target makes a Fortitude saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 the Monk’s class level + the Monk’s Wis modifier), it dies. If the saving throw is successful, the target is no longer in danger from that particular quivering palm attack, but it may still be affected by another one at a later time. Ki Strike: Adamantine (Su): The Monk’s unarmed blows are now considered adamantine for purposes of damage reduction and hardness penetration; the Monk’s unarmed attacks ignore the first 20 points of the target’s hardness. Timeless Body (Ex): The Monk no longer takes penalties to their ability scores for aging and cannot be magically aged. Any such penalties that have already been taken, however, remain in place. Bonuses still accrue, and the Monk still dies of old age when their time is up. Tongue of the Sun and Moon (Ex): The Monk can speak with any living creature. Empty Body (Su): The Monk gains the ability to assume an ethereal state for 1 round per Monk level per day, as though using the spell Etherealness. They may go ethereal on a number of different occasions during any single day, as long as the total number of rounds spent in an ethereal state does not exceed their Monk level. Perfect Self: At 20th level, the Monk becomes a magical creature. They are forevermore treated as an outsider rather than as a humanoid (or whatever the Monk’s creature type was) for the purpose of spells and magical effects. Additionally, the Monk gains damage reduction 10/magic, which allows them to ignore the first 10 points of damage from any attack made by a nonmagical weapon or by any natural attack made by a creature that doesn’t have similar damage reduction. Unlike other outsiders, the Monk can still be brought back from the dead as if they were a member of their previous creature type. Ex-Monks: A Monk who becomes nonlawful cannot gain new levels as a Monk but retains all Monk abilities. Like a member of any other class, a Monk may be a multiclass character, but multiclass Monks face a special 89 restriction; a Monk who gains a new class or (if already multiclass) raises another class by a level may never again raise their Monk level, though they retain all their Monk abilities. Paladin A holy warrior dedicated to a deity or principles of Law and Good, the Paladin has sworn an oath to uphold those principles. Actively venturing into the world to face the enemy head-on, the Paladin studies both the divine and the martial arts. Prerequisite: Divine Scale 1 or higher scenario, Lawful/Good alignment. Hit Die (of the Hero): d10 (d5+5) Action Points: Paladins gain a number of Action Points equal to their Charisma modifier [minimum +0, maximum +5] + one-half their character level, rounded down, at 1st level and every time they attain a new level in this class. Class Skills: The Paladin’s class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are: Concentration (Con), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Knowledge (nobility and royalty) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Knowledge (theology and philosophy), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), and Treat Injury (Wis). The Starting Occupation the character selects can provide additional class skills. Skill Points at 1st Level: (4 + Int modifier) x5. Skill Points at Each Additional Level: 4 + Int modifier. Starting Feats: In addition to the two feats all characters get at 1st level, a Paladin begins play with the Simple Weapons Proficiency feat, Martial Weapons Proficiency feat, Light Armor Proficiency, Medium Armor Proficiency, Heavy Armor Proficiency, and Shield Proficiency feats. Detect Evil (Sp): At will, a Paladin can use Detect Evil, as the spell. 90 Smite Evil (Su): Once per day, a Paladin may attempt to smite evil with one normal melee attack. If the Paladin accidentally smites a creature that is not evil, the smite has no effect, but the ability is still used up for that day. Divine Grace (Su): At 2nd level, a Paladin gains a bonus equal to their Charisma bonus (minimum +1) on all saving throws. Lay on Hands (Su): Beginning at 2nd level, a Paladin can heal wounds (their own or those of others) by touch. Each day they can heal a total number of hit points of damage equal to their Paladin level x their Charisma bonus (minimum x1). A Paladin may choose to divide their healing among multiple recipients, and they don’t have to use it all at once. Using lay on hands is a standard action. Alternatively, a Paladin can use any or all of this healing power to deal damage to undead creatures. Using lay on hands in this way requires a successful melee touch attack and doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity. The Paladin decides how many of their daily allotment of points to use as damage after successfully touching an undead creature. Aura of Courage (Su): Beginning at 3rd level, a Paladin is immune to fear (magical or otherwise). Each ally within 10 feet of the Paladin gains a +4 morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects. This ability functions while the Paladin is conscious, but not if they are unconscious or dead. Divine Health (Ex): At 3rd level, a Paladin gains immunity to all diseases, including supernatural and magical diseases. Turn Undead (Su): When a Paladin reaches 4th level, they gain the supernatural ability to turn undead. They may use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Charisma modifier. The Paladin turns undead as a Cleric of three levels lower would. Spells: Beginning at 4th level, a Paladin gains the ability to cast a small number of divine spells, only those from their god’s Domain lists. A Paladin casts their spells spontaneously, like a Saint. To be able cast a spell, a Paladin must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a Paladin’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the Paladin’s Wisdom or Charisma modifier, whichever is better. Like other spellcasters, a Paladin can cast only a certain number of spells per day. The Paladin’s base daily divine power point allotment is given on Table: Paladin Class Statistics by Level. In addition, they receive bonus power points per day if they have a high Wisdom or Charisma score, whichever is better. When Table: Paladin Class Statistics by Level indicates that the Paladin gets 0 power points per day, they gain only the bonus power points they would be entitled to based on their Wisdom or Charisma score, whichever is better. The Paladin does not receive any domain granted powers, as a Cleric does. Through 3rd level, a Paladin has no caster level. At 4th level and higher, their caster level is equal to one- half their Paladin level, rounded up. Furthermore, 6th-level spells only cost 10 power points for a 20th level (10th level spellcaster) Paladin. Special Mount (Sp): Upon reaching 5th level, a Paladin gains the service of an unusually intelligent, strong, and loyal steed to serve them in their crusade against evil (see “Animal Companions” below). This mount is usually a heavy warhorse (for a Medium Paladin) or a warpony (for a Small Paladin). However, in scenarios where a horse is not an ideal mount, other options may be discussed with your GM. The mount is fully trained, being capable of every trick listed under the Handle Animal skill description. Should the Paladin’s mount die, the Paladin may not summon another mount for thirty days or until they gain a Paladin level, whichever comes first, even if the mount is somehow returned from the dead. During this thirty-day period, the Paladin takes a –1 penalty on attack and weapon damage rolls. Remove Disease (Sp): At 6th level, a Paladin can produce a Remove Disease effect, as the spell, once per week. The Paladin can use this ability one additional time per week for every three levels after 6th (twice per week at 9th, three times at 12th, and so forth). A Paladin may also use an instance of Remove Disease to Lay on Hands (see above) for an amount of damage equal to their Paladin level plus their Cha modifier. Mettle (Ex): At 7th level, the Paladin’s strength of conviction is so great that they can slough off even the most dangerous effects. Whenever the Paladin makes a successful Fortitude or Will save against an effect that saves for “half” or “partial” effects, the Paladin instead negates the effect, ignoring it completely, with a successful save. Bonus Feat: At 10th level the Paladin gains a bonus feat; select any feat for which the Paladin qualifies. 91 Pious Grace: At 13th and 19th levels, the Paladin’s bonus to each of their saving throws from Divine Grace (see above) increases by +1. Favor of the Gods (Ex): At 16th level, the Paladin can elect to re-roll any d20 roll 1/day. They must, however, accept the result of the 2nd roll, even if it’s worse than the first (their god has spoken!). Code of Conduct: A Paladin must be of lawful good alignment and loses all class abilities if they ever willingly commit an evil act. Additionally, a Paladin’s code requires that they respect legitimate authority, act with honor (not lying, not cheating, not using poison, and so forth), help those in need (provided they do not use the help for evil or chaotic ends), and punish those who harm or threaten innocents. Associates: While they may adventure with characters of any good or neutral alignment, a Paladin will never knowingly associate with evil characters, nor will they continue an association with someone who consistently offends their moral code. A Paladin may accept only henchmen, followers, or cohorts who are lawful good. Ex-Paladins: A Paladin who ceases to be Lawful Good, who willfully commits an evil act, or who grossly violates the code of conduct loses all Paladin spells and abilities (including the service of the Paladin’s mount, but not weapon, armor, and shield proficiencies). They may not progress any farther in levels as a Paladin. They regain their abilities and advancement potential if they atone for their violations (see the Atonement spell description), as appropriate. Like a member of any other class, a Paladin may be a multiclass character, but multiclass Paladins face a special restriction; a Paladin who gains a level in any class other than Paladin may never again raise their Paladin level, though they retain all their Paladin abilities. Power Points/Day: A Psion’s ability to manifest powers is limited by the power points they have available. The Psion’s base daily psionic power point allotment is given on Table: Psion Class Statistics by Level. In addition, they receive bonus power points per day if they have an Intelligence score of 12 or higher. The Psion’s race may also provide bonus power points per day, as may certain feats and items. Discipline: A discipline is one of six groupings of powers, each defined by a common theme. The six disciplines are clairsentience, metacreativity, psychokinesis, psychometabolism, psychoportation, and telepathy. Clairsentience: A Psion who chooses clairsentience is known as a Seer. Seers can learn precognitive powers to aid their comrades in combat, as well as powers that permit them to gather information in many different ways. Metacreativity: A Psion specializing in metacreativity is known as a Shaper. This discipline includes powers that draw ectoplasm or matter from the Astral Plane, creating semisolid and solid items such as armor, weapons, or animated constructs to do battle at the shaper’s command. Psychokinesis: A Psion who specializes in psychokinesis is known as a Kineticist. They are the masters of powers that manipulate and transform matter and energy. Kineticists can attack with devastating blasts of energy. Psychometabolism: A Psion who specializes in psychometabolism is known as an Egoist. This discipline consists of powers that alter the Psion’s psychobiology, or that of creatures near them. An egoist can both heal and transform themselves into a fearsome fighter. Psychoportation: A Psion who relies on psychoportation powers is known as a Nomad. Nomads can wield powers that propel or displace objects in space or time. Telepathy: A Psion who chooses the discipline of telepathy is known as a Telepath. They are masters of powers that allow mental contact and control of other sentient creatures. A telepath can deceive or destroy the minds of their enemies with ease. Every Psion must decide at 1st level which psionic discipline they will specialize in. Choosing a discipline provides a Psion with access to the class skills associated with that discipline (see above), as well as the powers restricted to that discipline. However, choosing a discipline also means that the Psion cannot learn powers that are restricted to other disciplines. They can’t even use such powers by employing psionic items. Powers Known: A Psion begins play knowing three 1st-level Psion powers of your choice. Each time they achieve a new level, they unlock the knowledge of new powers. Choose the powers known from the Psion power list, or from the list of powers of your chosen discipline. You cannot choose powers from disciplines other than your chosen discipline. (Exception: The feat Expanded Knowledge allows a Psion to learn powers from the lists of other disciplines or even other classes.) A Psion can manifest any power that has a power point cost equal to or lower than their manifester level. The number of times a Psion can manifest powers in a day is limited only by their daily power points. A Psion simply knows their powers; they are ingrained in the Psion’s mind. The Psion does not need to 93 prepare them (in the way that some spellcasters prepare their spells), though they must get a good night’s sleep each day to regain all their spent power points. The Difficulty Class for saving throws against Psion powers is 10 + the power’s level + the Psion’s Intelligence modifier. Maximum Power Level Known: A Psion begins play with the ability to learn 1st-level powers. As they attain higher levels, a Psion may gain the ability to master more complex powers, with the option to learn new powers up to, but not necessarily at, their maximum known power level. To learn or manifest a power, a Psion must have an Intelligence score of at least 10 + the power’s level. The typical domestic animal has a starting attitude of indifferent, while wild animals are usually unfriendly. To use Wild Empathy, the Ranger and the animal must be able to study each other, which means that they must be within 30 feet of one another under normal visibility conditions. Combat Style (Ex): At 2nd level, a Ranger must select one of two combat styles to pursue: ranged or two-weapon combat. The Rogue cannot use a weapon that deals lethal damage to deal nonlethal damage in a Sneak Attack, not even with the usual –4 penalty. 98 A Rogue can Sneak Attack only living creatures with discernible anatomies—undead, constructs, oozes, plants, and incorporeal creatures lack vital areas to attack. Any creature that is immune to critical hits is not vulnerable to sneak attacks. The Rogue must be able to see the target well enough to pick out a vital spot and must be able to reach such a spot. A Rogue cannot Sneak Attack while striking a creature with concealment or striking the limbs of a creature whose vitals are beyond reach. Trapfinding: Rogues (and only Rogues) can use the Search skill to locate traps when the task has a Difficulty Class higher than 20. Finding a nonmagical trap has a DC of at least 20, or higher if it is well hidden. Finding a magic/psionic trap has a DC of 25 + the level of the spell or power used to create it. Rogues (and only Rogues) can use the Disable Device skill to disarm magic/psionic traps. A magic/psionic trap generally has a DC of 25 + the level of the spell or power used to create it. A Rogue who beats a trap’s DC by 10 or more with a Disable Device check can study a trap, figure out how it works, and bypass it (with their party) without disarming it. Evasion (Ex): At 2nd level and higher, a Rogue can avoid even magical and unusual attacks with great agility. If the Rogue makes a successful Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, they instead take no damage. Evasion can be used only if the Rogue is wearing light armor or no armor. A helpless Rogue does not gain the benefit of Evasion. Trap Sense (Ex): At 3rd level, a Rogue gains an intuitive sense that alerts them to danger from traps, giving them a +1 bonus on Reflex saves made to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to AC against attacks made by traps. These bonuses rise to +2 when the Rogue reaches 6th level, to +3 when they reach 9th level, to +4 when they reach 12th level, to +5 at 15th, and to +6 at 18th level. Trap Sense bonuses gained from multiple classes stack. Uncanny Dodge (Ex): Starting at 4th level, a Rogue can react to danger before their senses would normally allow them to do so. They retain their Dexterity bonus to AC (if any) even if they are caught flat-footed or struck by an invisible attacker. However, the Rogue still loses their Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. If a Rogue already has Uncanny Dodge from a different class they automatically gain Improved Uncanny Dodge (see below) instead. Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex): A Rogue of 8th level or higher can no longer be flanked. This defense denies another Rogue the ability to sneak attack the character by flanking them, unless the attacker has at least four more Rogue levels than the target does. An opponent damaged by such a Sneak Attacks also takes 2 points of Strength damage. Ability points lost to damage return on their own at the rate of 1 point per day for each damaged ability. Defensive Roll (Ex): The Rogue can roll with a potentially lethal blow to take less damage from it than they otherwise would. To use this ability, the Rogue must attempt a Dodge (DC = damage dealt). If the Defensive Roll succeeds, they take only half damage from the blow; if it fails, they take full damage. The Rogue must be aware of the attack and able to react to it in order to execute the defensive roll—if the Rogue is denied their Dexterity bonus to AC, they can’t use this ability. Improved Evasion (Ex): This ability works like Evasion, except that while the Rogue still takes no damage on a successful Reflex saving throw against attacks; henceforth the Rogue takes only half damage on a failed save. A helpless Rogue (ie. one denied their Dexterity bonus to AC) does not gain the benefit of Improved Evasion. Opportunist (Ex): Once per round, the Rogue can make an attack of opportunity against an opponent who has just been struck for damage in melee by another character. This attack counts as the Rogue’s attack of opportunity for that round. Even a Rogue with the Combat Reflexes feat can’t use the Opportunist ability more than once per round. Skill Mastery: The Rogue becomes so certain in the use of certain skills that they can use them reliably even under 99 adverse conditions. Upon gaining this ability, the Rogue selects a number of skills equal to 3 + their Intelligence modifier. A Rogue may gain this special ability multiple times, selecting additional skills for it to apply to each time. Slippery Mind (Ex): This ability represents the Rogue’s ability to wriggle free from mind-affecting effects that would otherwise control or compel her. The Rogue gets only this one extra chance to succeed on their saving throw. Bonus Feat: A Rogue may gain a bonus feat in place of a special ability. The feat may be any feat that the Rogue qualifies for. Improved Evasion: At 14th level the Rogue has mastered the art of evading area-effect attacks; with the same limitations as Evasion, the character only takes half damage even on a failed Reflex saving throw for half damage. At 2nd level, the Saint gains a 1st-level spell or power as a supernatural ability, usable 3/day or for its regular point cost. The spell or power chosen must be one that would be an aspect of their deity’s domains. At 7th level, the Saint gains a 2nd- or 3rd-level spell or power as a supernatural ability, usable 2/day or for its regular point cost. The spell or power chosen must be one that would be an aspect of their deity’s domains. At 13th level, the Saint gains a 4th-, 5th-, or 6th-level spell or power as a supernatural ability, usable 1/day or for its regular point cost. The spell or power chosen must be one that would be an aspect of their deity’s domains. At 19th level, the Saint gains the supernatural power to perform a Miracle 1/day. Note that this ability never costs the Saint any experience points (but as always it is privy to their deity’s will / GM’s discretion). Personal Domain: Starting at 3rd level and every other level thereafter, the Saint begins to build a Personal Domain spell list, as approved by their deity (ie. the GM). The Saint may add one spell of their choice, up to their maximum spell level, from the Cleric spell list. If the GM allows the selection, then the Saint adds the Cleric spell to their list of spells known. Like the domain spells, these additions are permanent additions to the Saint’s spell list and cannot be changed once chosen and approved. Note that in the cases of certain Domains, like the Animal and/or Plant domains, the Magic domain, or the 101 Mind domain, it may be permissible for the Saint’s deity to grant a spell from the Druid spell list, or the Sorcerer / Wizard spell list, or a power from the Psion / Wilder power list, respectively. Your GM will determine if your god is feeling generous... True Sainthood (Divine Rank 0): At 20th level, the devoted Saint ascends (or descends) into the eternal service of their god, becoming a Hero with Divine Rank 0 (ask your GM about Divine Ranks). Amongst other things, this means that the Saint becomes an Outsider. As an Outsider the Saint now possesses the following traits; —Darkvision out to 60 feet. —Unlike most other living creatures, an outsider does not have a dual nature—its soul and body form one unit. When an outsider is slain, no soul is set loose, instead returning to its plane of origin. Spells that restore souls to their bodies, such as Raise Dead, Reincarnate, and Resurrection, don’t work on an Outsider. It takes a different magical effect, such as a Miracle, a Reality Revision, a Wish, or a True Resurrection to restore it to the Prime Material Plane. —Proficient with all simple and martial weapons and any weapons mentioned in its entry. —Proficient with whatever types of armor (light, medium, or heavy) it has the proficiencies for. Outsiders are also proficient with shields if they are proficient with any form of armor. —Outsiders breathe, but do not need to eat or sleep (although they can do so if they wish). Also, as a sign of their god’s favor, the Saint receives a +4 inherent bonus to the attribute of their choice. Ex-Saints (“Anathema”): A Saint who grossly violates the code of conduct required by their god loses all spells and class features, except for armor and weapon proficiencies. They cannot thereafter gain levels as a Saint or Cleric of that god until they atone (see the Atonement spell description). Representatives of the ex-Saint’s god may seek retribution for the violation (GM’s choice). Sorcerer Innately gifted with arcane power, each Sorcerer is unique, with their own personal array of spells. One thing all Sorcerers have in common is a Familiar, an animal ally with whom they share a powerful connection. Campaign Prerequisites: Minimum Arcane Scale 1 scenario. Hit Die (of the Hero): d4 (d2+2) Action Points: Sorcerers gain a number of Action Points equal to their Charisma modifier [minimum +0, maximum +5] + one-half their character level, rounded down, at 1st level and every time they attain a new level in this class. Class Skills: The Sorcerer’s class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are: Bluff (Cha), Concentration (Con), Craft (Int), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Profession (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int).
